newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes at 20-month high vs dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes at 20-month high vs dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up on speculative buying against the U.S. dollar at an intraday high of 8.2945 on Thursday, up from 8.2962 on Wednesday, its highest closing rate for 20 months, traders said.
It was the highest closing level since May 19, 1995 when it ended at 8.2928.

Dealers said the yuan moved within a stable band before a sharp rise before the close. The People's Bank of China announcement of the February interest rate subsidy for bank deposits of three or more years at 2.09 percent, down from 2.87 percent for January, had no effect on trading, they said.
The yuan opened higher at 8.2956 and consolidated near the opening level and at an intraday low of 8.2959 for almost the whole day's trading before its rise just before the close.
Trading was less active than on Wednesday with most done at 8.2957, traders said.
One dealer said the yuan's rise late in trading had little impact on its stability.
"Although the pro-yuan sentiment was stronger, it would not stand firm at such a high level tomorrow," he said.
A second dealer said a few Chinese banks were seen buying dollars to bolster their foreign exchange reserves, capping the yuan's uptrend.
"Fear of central bank intervention in the market at higher prices also capped the yuan's rise," he said.
Dealers expected the yuan to drop to around 8.2960 on Friday.
The yuan closed down at 7.0931 from 7.0779 against 100 Japanese yen and up at an intraday high of 1.0715 from 1.0724 against the Hong Kong dollar.
